body:
# the contributor audit: all-dimensional simplex-container obstruction


specified compatibility-cost lemma; it is not an OC counterexample.
I read `candidate a585520b0a2a14db`
in full and independently checked the following geometric steps.

The three original fibers A, P/2, B are actual fibers of their convex
hull because A+B is contained in P; its projection is exactly[0,2].
All have positive d-volume and the hull has ambient interior. The
barycentric apex cap of the enclosing standard simplex bounds the
maximum cap mass of A by Gamma_d V. Subtracting Gamma_d|A| yields
the claimed deficit at most Gamma_d epsilon^d V. The paired maximum
is at most the ordinary maximum, since zero shift is allowed. Its
centroid lower bound makes the paired deficit nonnegative. The two
other fibers are simplices and have zero deficits.

For an arbitrary simplex R containing A, cones over the actual
coordinate facets and the upper facet give x_i>=-delta and
sum x_i<=1+delta for EVERY point of R. If the volume excess is less
than epsilon V/(16d^2), then delta<epsilon/(8d^2) and d delta<epsilon/16.
The d vertices with a coordinate at least one must be distinct; their
coordinate sums exceed epsilon. The remaining vertex v_0 has sum
at most epsilon, since epsilon e_i belongs to R.

The barycentric representation of epsilon e_i has positive v_0
coefficient. Its coordinate-sum bound gives the displayed upper
bound for (1-alpha_0)/alpha_0. For each coordinate j choose i!=j;
the coordinate lower bounds then imply
sum_j(v_0)_j <= d delta(epsilon+d delta)/(1-epsilon-d delta)
<epsilon^2/4<epsilon/2. This works for all rotations and translations
of R and imposes no hidden simplex-contact condition.

The cone from v_0 over the full lower facet of P lies outside P
except for its base. Its exact volume is
V(da-epsilon)^(d-1)(epsilon-sum v_0). Scaling the middle fiber by two
accounts for the factor 2^-d. The resulting excess is at least
epsilon V/8, which exceeds the desired epsilon V/(16d^2).
Every convexified middle container contains P/2 and R_0/2, because
the last endpoint container contains the origin. Thus the nested
lemma applies to every jointly chosen family of simplex containers.

Adding an exposed second integer layer with three equal-volume
simplex fibers preserves every lower-layer fiber exactly. Its total
mass W exceeds four times the maximum fiber mass F. Further binary
padding preserves each exposed layer and multiplies both deficit
and required added mass equally. Hence the no-heavy claim is valid
for every n>=2, with threshold 2^-n. No new integer projections or
intrinsic-measure degeneracies occur.

The exact standard-library verifier returned PASS for 72 rational
source/constant/no-heavy cases, 120 independently perturbed enclosing
simplices, and 102 small-excess vertex/pyramid certificates. These
checks supplement the uniform proof above.

Thus replacing the ordinary deficits by the newly studied paired
deficits does not repair this proposed compatibility-cost bridge in
any d>=2. A different mixed mechanism is necessary.
